quotes.text_ko: 말로 표현할 수 있는 도는 영원한 도가 아니며, 이름 붙일 수 있는 이름은 영원한 이름이 아니다.
quotes.text_source_en: The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao. The name that can be named is not the enduring and unchanging name.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 세상 사람들이 아름다움을 아름답다고 아는 순간 추함도 생겨나고, 능숙함을 능숙하다고 아는 순간 서투름도 생겨난다.
quotes.text_source_en: All in the world know the beauty of the beautiful, and in doing this they have (the idea of) what ugliness is; they all know the skill of the skilful, and in doing this they have (the idea of) what the want of skill is.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 뛰어난 이를 지나치게 떠받들지 않으면 사람들이 다투지 않고, 얻기 어려운 물건을 귀히 여기지 않으면 도둑이 생기지 않으며, 욕망을 자극할 것을 드러내지 않으면 마음이 어지럽지 않다.
quotes.text_source_en: Not to value and employ men of superior ability is the way to keep the people from rivalry among themselves; not to prize articles which are difficult to procure is the way to keep them from becoming thieves; not to show them what is likely to excite their desires is the way to keep their minds from disorder.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 도는 텅 빈 그릇과 같아 써도 가득 차지 않는다. 그 깊이를 헤아릴 수 없으니 만물의 근원인 듯하다.
quotes.text_source_en: The Tao is (like) the emptiness of a vessel; and in our employment of it we must be on our guard against all fulness. How deep and unfathomable it is, as if it were the Honoured Ancestor of all things!
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 하늘과 땅은 사사로운 인자함으로 움직이지 않고 만물을 풀로 만든 제물처럼 대한다. 성인도 사사로운 인자함에 매이지 않고 백성을 같은 이치로 대한다.
quotes.text_source_en: Heaven and earth do not act from (the impulse of) any wish to be benevolent; they deal with all things as the dogs of grass are dealt with. The sages do not act from (any wish to be) benevolent; they deal with the people as the dogs of grass are dealt with.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 골짜기의 신은 죽지 않으며 이를 신비로운 암컷이라 한다. 그 문은 하늘과 땅의 뿌리이며, 끊임없이 이어져 부드럽게 써도 다하지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: The valley spirit dies not, aye the same; The female mystery thus do we name. Its gate, from which at first they issued forth, Is called the root from which grew heaven and earth. Long and unbroken does its power remain, Used gently, and without the touch of pain.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 하늘은 오래고 땅은 영원하다. 하늘과 땅이 오래가는 까닭은 자신만을 위해 살지 않기 때문이다.
quotes.text_source_en: Heaven is long-enduring and earth continues long. The reason why heaven and earth are able to endure and continue thus long is because they do not live of, or for, themselves. This is how they are able to continue and endure.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 가장 높은 선은 물과 같다. 물은 만물을 이롭게 하면서도 다투지 않고, 사람들이 꺼리는 낮은 곳에 머무르므로 도에 가깝다.
quotes.text_source_en: The highest excellence is like (that of) water. The excellence of water appears in its benefiting all things, and in its occupying, without striving (to the contrary), the low place which all men dislike. Hence (its way) is near to (that of) the Tao.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 그릇은 가득 채운 채 들고 있기보다 적당히 비워 두는 편이 낫다. 날을 계속 세우면 그 날카로움을 오래 보존할 수 없다.
quotes.text_source_en: It is better to leave a vessel unfilled, than to attempt to carry it when it is full. If you keep feeling a point that has been sharpened, the point cannot long preserve its sharpness.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 정신과 몸을 하나로 품어 흩어지지 않게 할 수 있는가. 숨을 온전히 다스려 갓난아이처럼 부드러워지고, 마음의 흐린 영상을 씻어 흠 없이 될 수 있는가.
quotes.text_source_en: When the intelligent and animal souls are held together in one embrace, they can be kept from separating. When one gives undivided attention to the (vital) breath, and brings it to the utmost degree of pliancy, he can become as a (tender) babe. When he has cleansed away the most mysterious sights (of his imagination), he can become without a flaw.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 서른 개의 바퀴살은 빈 축을 중심으로 모이고, 그릇과 방도 비어 있는 곳 때문에 쓸모가 생긴다. 있는 것은 이로움을 주고, 없는 것은 쓰임을 만든다.
quotes.text_source_en: The thirty spokes unite in the one nave; but it is on the empty space (for the axle), that the use of the wheel depends. Clay is fashioned into vessels; but it is on their empty hollowness, that their use depends. The door and windows are cut out (from the walls) to form an apartment; but it is on the empty space (within), that its use depends. Therefore, what has a (positive) existence serves for profitable adaptation, and what has not that for (actual) usefulness.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 화려한 빛깔은 눈을 멀게 하고, 지나친 음악은 귀를 둔하게 하며, 강한 맛은 입맛을 해친다. 격렬한 사냥과 희귀한 물건에 대한 탐욕은 마음과 행동을 어지럽힌다.
quotes.text_source_en: Colour's five hues from th' eyes their sight will take; Music's five notes the ears as deaf can make; The flavours five deprive the mouth of taste; The chariot course, and the wild hunting waste Make mad the mind; and objects rare and strange, Sought for, men's conduct will to evil change.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 총애와 모욕은 모두 두려움의 근원이 되고, 명예와 큰 재난도 자신에게 닥친 일처럼 보아야 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: Favour and disgrace would seem equally to be feared; honour and great calamity, to be regarded as personal conditions (of the same kind).
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 보려 해도 보이지 않아 평평하다 하고, 들으려 해도 들리지 않아 고요하다 하며, 잡으려 해도 잡히지 않아 미묘하다 한다. 이 셋은 설명할 수 없으므로 하나라 부른다.
quotes.text_source_en: We look at it, and we do not see it, and we name it 'the Equable.' We listen to it, and we do not hear it, and we name it 'the Inaudible.' We try to grasp it, and do not get hold of it, and we name it 'the Subtle.' With these three qualities, it cannot be made the subject of description; and hence we blend them together and obtain The One.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 옛날 도에 능한 사람들은 미묘하고 깊어 그 속을 헤아릴 수 없었다. 헤아릴 수 없기에 그 모습만 애써 묘사할 뿐이다.
quotes.text_source_en: The skilful masters (of the Tao) in old times, with a subtle and exquisite penetration, comprehended its mysteries, and were deep (also) so as to elude men's knowledge. As they were thus beyond men's knowledge, I will make an effort to describe of what sort they appeared to be.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 비움을 극진히 하고 고요함을 굳게 지켜라. 만물은 왕성히 움직인 뒤 각자 뿌리로 돌아가며, 뿌리로 돌아가는 것을 고요함이라 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: The (state of) vacancy should be brought to the utmost degree, and that of stillness guarded with unwearying vigour. All things alike go through their processes of activity, and (then) we see them return (to their original state). When things (in the vegetable world) have displayed their luxuriant growth, we see each of them return to its root. This returning to their root is what we call the state of stillness; and that stillness may be called a reporting that they have fulfilled their appointed end.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 가장 훌륭한 통치자는 백성이 그 존재를 거의 알지 못한다. 그다음은 사랑하고 칭송받는 자이며, 그다음은 두려움의 대상이고, 가장 못한 자는 업신여김을 받는다.
quotes.text_source_en: In the highest antiquity, (the people) did not know that there were (their rulers). In the next age they loved them and praised them. In the next they feared them; in the next they despised them. Thus it was that when faith (in the Tao) was deficient (in the rulers) a want of faith in them ensued (in the people).
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 큰 도가 사라진 뒤에야 인과 의가 내세워졌고, 지혜와 영리함이 드러나자 큰 위선이 뒤따랐다.
quotes.text_source_en: When the Great Tao (Way or Method) ceased to be observed, benevolence and righteousness came into vogue. (Then) appeared wisdom and shrewdness, and there ensued great hypocrisy.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 성스러움을 버리고 지혜를 내려놓으면 백성에게 백 배 이롭다. 인과 의를 내세우지 않으면 효도와 자애가 돌아오고, 교묘한 꾀와 이익을 버리면 도둑이 사라진다.
quotes.text_source_en: If we could renounce our sageness and discard our wisdom, it would be better for the people a hundredfold. If we could renounce our benevolence and discard our righteousness, the people would again become filial and kindly. If we could renounce our artful contrivances and discard our (scheming for) gain, there would be no thieves nor robbers.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 억지로 배우려는 집착을 내려놓으면 근심이 줄어든다. 사람들이 두려워하는 것은 두려워해야 하지만, 따져야 할 문제는 끝없이 넓다.
quotes.text_source_en: When we renounce learning we have no troubles. The (ready) 'yes,' and (flattering) 'yea;'-- Small is the difference they display. But mark their issues, good and ill;-- What space the gulf between shall fill? What all men fear is indeed to be feared; but how wide and without end is the range of questions (asking to be discussed)!
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 큰 덕의 모습은 오직 도를 따른다. 도는 보이지 않고 잡히지 않지만 그 안에 만물의 형상과 본질이 있으며, 예로부터 지금까지 사라지지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: The grandest forms of active force From Tao come, their only source. Who can of Tao the nature tell? Our sight it flies, our touch as well. Eluding sight, eluding touch, The forms of things all in it crouch; Eluding touch, eluding sight, There are their semblances, all right. Profound it is, dark and obscure; Things' essences all there endure. Those essences the truth enfold Of what, when seen, shall then be told. Now it is so; 'twas so of old. Its name--what passes not away; So, in their beautiful array, Things form and never know decay. How know I that it is so with all the beauties of existing things? By this (nature of the Tao).
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 굽은 것은 온전해지고, 휜 것은 곧아지며, 빈 것은 채워지고, 낡은 것은 새로워진다. 욕심이 적으면 얻고, 욕심이 많으면 길을 잃는다.
quotes.text_source_en: The partial becomes complete; the crooked, straight; the empty, full; the worn out, new. He whose (desires) are few gets them; he whose (desires) are many goes astray.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 말을 줄이는 것은 자연을 따르는 일이다. 거센 바람도 아침 내내 불지 않고 폭우도 하루 종일 내리지 않으니, 하늘과 땅도 급격한 작용을 오래 지속하지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: Abstaining from speech marks him who is obeying the spontaneity of his nature. A violent wind does not last for a whole morning; a sudden rain does not last for the whole day. To whom is it that these (two) things are owing? To Heaven and Earth. If Heaven and Earth cannot make such (spasmodic) actings last long, how much less can man!
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 발끝으로 선 사람은 오래 서지 못하고, 보폭을 과하게 넓힌 사람은 제대로 걷지 못한다. 자신을 드러내고 자랑하는 사람도 도의 관점에서는 불필요한 군더더기와 같다.
quotes.text_source_en: He who stands on his tiptoes does not stand firm; he who stretches his legs does not walk (easily). (So), he who displays himself does not shine; he who asserts his own views is not distinguished; he who vaunts himself does not find his merit acknowledged; he who is self-conceited has no superiority allowed to him. Such conditions, viewed from the standpoint of the Tao, are like remnants of food, or a tumour on the body, which all dislike. Hence those who pursue (the course) of the Tao do not adopt and allow them.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 하늘과 땅보다 먼저 생겨난, 분별할 수 없으나 완전한 무엇이 있었다. 고요하고 형체가 없으며 홀로 서서 변하지 않고, 어디에나 미치면서도 다하지 않으니 만물의 어머니라 할 수 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: There was something undefined and complete, coming into existence before Heaven and Earth. How still it was and formless, standing alone, and undergoing no change, reaching everywhere and in no danger (of being exhausted)! It may be regarded as the Mother of all things.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 무거움은 가벼움의 뿌리이고, 고요함은 움직임의 주인이다.
quotes.text_source_en: Gravity is the root of lightness; stillness, the ruler of movement.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 능숙한 여행자는 자취를 남기지 않고, 능숙한 말은 흠잡을 곳이 없으며, 능숙한 사람은 누구도 버리지 않는다. 이것을 밝음을 감추는 지혜라 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: The skilful traveller leaves no traces of his wheels or footsteps; the skilful speaker says nothing that can be found fault with or blamed; the skilful reckoner uses no tallies; the skilful closer needs no bolts or bars, while to open what he has shut will be impossible; the skilful binder uses no strings or knots, while to unloose what he has bound will be impossible. In the same way the sage is always skilful at saving men, and so he does not cast away any man; he is always skilful at saving things, and so he does not cast away anything. This is called 'Hiding the light of his procedure.'
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 자신의 강함을 알면서도 부드러움을 지키면 세상의 계곡이 된다. 밝음을 알면서도 어둠 속에 머물고, 영광을 알면서도 낮은 자리를 사랑하면 본래의 소박함으로 돌아간다.
quotes.text_source_en: Who knows his manhood's strength, Yet still his female feebleness maintains; As to one channel flow the many drains, All come to him, yea, all beneath the sky. Thus he the constant excellence retains; The simple child again, free from all stains. Who knows how white attracts, Yet always keeps himself within black's shade, The pattern of humility displayed, Displayed in view of all beneath the sky; He in the unchanging excellence arrayed, Endless return to man's first state has made. Who knows how glory shines, Yet loves disgrace, nor e'er for it is pale; Behold his presence in a spacious vale, To which men come from all beneath the sky. The unchanging excellence completes its tale; The simple infant man in him we hail.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 세상을 차지하려고 억지로 움직이는 사람은 성공하지 못한다. 세상은 신묘한 것이어서 강제로 다룰 수 없으며, 붙잡으려 하면 잃고 조종하려 하면 망친다.
quotes.text_source_en: If any one should wish to get the kingdom for himself, and to effect this by what he does, I see that he will not succeed. The kingdom is a spirit-like thing, and cannot be got by active doing. He who would so win it destroys it; he who would hold it in his grasp loses it.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 도에 따라 군주를 돕는 사람은 무력으로 세상을 제압하려 하지 않는다. 힘으로 한 일은 반드시 그에 따른 대가를 부른다.
quotes.text_source_en: He who would assist a lord of men in harmony with the Tao will not assert his mastery in the kingdom by force of arms. Such a course is sure to meet with its proper return.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 무기는 아름답게 꾸며도 불길한 도구이며 모든 생명이 싫어하는 것이다. 도를 따르는 사람은 부득이한 경우가 아니면 사용하지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: Now arms, however beautiful, are instruments of evil omen, hateful, it may be said, to all creatures. Therefore they who have the Tao do not like to employ them.

quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics

quotes.text_ko: 변하지 않는 도에는 이름이 없다.

quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics

quotes.text_ko: 남을 아는 사람은 분별력이 있고 자신을 아는 사람은 밝다. 남을 이기는 사람은 힘이 세지만 자신을 이기는 사람은 참으로 강하다.
quotes.text_source_en: He who knows other men is discerning; he who knows himself is intelligent. He who overcomes others is strong; he who overcomes himself is mighty. He who is satisfied with his lot is rich; he who goes on acting with energy has a (firm) will.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics

quotes.text_ko: 큰 도는 사방으로 흘러 어디에나 미친다. 만물은 그것에 기대어 생기지만 도는 주인 행세를 하지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: All-pervading is the Great Tao! It may be found on the left hand and on the right.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 큰 형상을 붙들면 세상 사람들이 찾아오고, 찾아온 이들은 해를 입지 않고 평안과 고요를 얻는다.
quotes.text_source_en: To him who holds in his hands the Great Image (of the invisible Tao), the whole world repairs. Men resort to him, and receive no hurt, but (find) rest, peace, and the feeling of ease.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 무언가를 줄이려면 먼저 펴 주고, 약하게 하려면 먼저 강하게 하며, 빼앗으려면 먼저 주어야 한다. 부드럽고 약한 것이 굳세고 강한 것을 이긴다.
quotes.text_source_en: When one is about to take an inspiration, he is sure to make a (previous) expiration; when he is going to weaken another, he will first strengthen him; when he is going to overthrow another, he will first have raised him up; when he is going to despoil another, he will first have made gifts to him:--this is called 'Hiding the light (of his procedure).'
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 도는 언제나 억지로 행하지 않지만 이루지 못하는 일이 없다.
quotes.text_source_en: The Tao in its regular course does nothing (for the sake of doing it), and so there is nothing which it does not do.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 높은 덕을 지닌 사람은 자신의 덕을 드러내려 하지 않으므로 참된 덕을 지닌다. 낮은 덕의 사람은 덕을 잃지 않으려 애쓰기에 오히려 온전한 덕을 잃는다.
quotes.text_source_en: (Those who) possessed in highest degree the attributes (of the Tao) did not (seek) to show them, and therefore they possessed them (in fullest measure). (Those who) possessed in a lower degree those attributes (sought how) not to lose them, and therefore they did not possess them (in fullest measure).
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics

quotes.text_ko: 예로부터 하나를 얻은 하늘은 맑고, 땅은 안정되며, 골짜기는 차고, 만물은 살아나고, 군주는 세상의 기준이 되었다.
quotes.text_source_en: The things which from of old have got the One (the Tao) are-- Heaven which by it is bright and pure; Earth rendered thereby firm and sure; Spirits with powers by it supplied; Valleys kept full throughout their void All creatures which through it do live Princes and kings who from it get The model which to all they give. All these are the results of the One (Tao).
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 도의 움직임은 되돌아감이고, 도가 작용하는 방식은 부드러움이다.
quotes.text_source_en: The movement of the Tao By contraries proceeds; And weakness marks the course Of Tao's mighty deeds.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 가장 뛰어난 사람은 도를 들으면 부지런히 실천하고, 중간 사람은 믿었다 의심하며, 가장 낮은 사람은 크게 비웃는다. 비웃음을 받지 않는다면 도라 할 수 없다.
quotes.text_source_en: Scholars of the highest class, when they hear about the Tao, earnestly carry it into practice. Scholars of the middle class, when they have heard about it, seem now to keep it and now to lose it. Scholars of the lowest class, when they have heard about it, laugh greatly at it. If it were not (thus) laughed at, it would not be fit to be the Tao.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 도는 하나를 낳고, 하나는 둘을 낳으며, 둘은 셋을 낳고, 셋은 만물을 낳는다. 만물은 음을 등에 지고 양을 품으며 빈 기운으로 조화를 이룬다.
quotes.text_source_en: The Tao produced One; One produced Two; Two produced Three; Three produced All things. All things leave behind them the Obscurity (out of which they have come), and go forward to embrace the Brightness (into which they have emerged), while they are harmonised by the Breath of Vacancy.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 세상에서 가장 부드러운 것이 가장 단단한 것을 이기고, 형체 없는 것이 틈 없는 곳으로 들어간다. 이로써 억지로 하지 않는 것의 이로움을 안다.
quotes.text_source_en: The softest thing in the world dashes against and overcomes the hardest; that which has no (substantial) existence enters where there is no crevice. I know hereby what advantage belongs to doing nothing (with a purpose).
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 명성과 생명 가운데 무엇이 더 소중한가. 생명과 재물 가운데 무엇을 택할 것인가. 얻는 것과 잃는 것 중 무엇이 더 큰 고통을 부르는가.
quotes.text_source_en: Or fame or life, Which do you hold more dear? Or life or wealth, To which would you adhere? Keep life and lose those other things; Keep them and lose your life:--which brings Sorrow and pain more near?
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 큰 완성은 모자란 듯 보여도 그 쓰임이 다하지 않고, 큰 충만은 빈 듯 보여도 고갈되지 않는다. 가장 곧은 것은 굽은 듯하고, 큰 솜씨는 서툰 듯하며, 큰 말재주는 더듬는 듯하다.
quotes.text_source_en: Who thinks his great achievements poor Shall find his vigour long endure. Of greatest fulness, deemed a void, Exhaustion ne'er shall stem the tide. Do thou what's straight still crooked deem; Thy greatest art still stupid seem, And eloquence a stammering scream.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 세상에 도가 행해지면 전쟁용 말이 밭을 갈고, 도가 사라지면 군마가 국경에서 새끼를 낳는다.
quotes.text_source_en: When the Tao prevails in the world, they send back their swift horses to (draw) the dung-carts. When the Tao is disregarded in the world, the war-horses breed in the border lands.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 문밖으로 나가지 않고도 세상을 이해하며, 창밖을 보지 않고도 하늘의 도를 볼 수 있다. 자신에게서 멀리 나갈수록 아는 것은 오히려 줄어든다.
quotes.text_source_en: Without going outside his door, one understands (all that takes place) under the sky; without looking out from his window, one sees the Tao of Heaven. The farther that one goes out (from himself), the less he knows.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 학문을 닦는 사람은 날마다 지식을 더하고, 도를 닦는 사람은 날마다 억지로 하는 일을 덜어 낸다.
quotes.text_source_en: He who devotes himself to learning (seeks) from day to day to increase (his knowledge); he who devotes himself to the Tao (seeks) from day to day to diminish (his doing).
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 성인은 고정된 자기 마음을 고집하지 않고 백성의 마음을 자신의 마음으로 삼는다.
quotes.text_source_en: The sage has no invariable mind of his own; he makes the mind of the people his mind.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 사람은 태어나 삶으로 나오고, 죽어 다시 들어간다.
quotes.text_source_en: Men come forth and live; they enter (again) and die.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 만물은 도에서 생겨나고 덕의 작용으로 길러지며, 저마다의 성질에 따라 형체를 얻고 처한 환경에 따라 완성된다. 그래서 만물은 도를 높이고 덕을 귀하게 여긴다.
quotes.text_source_en: All things are produced by the Tao, and nourished by its outflowing operation. They receive their forms according to the nature of each, and are completed according to the circumstances of their condition. Therefore all things without exception honour the Tao, and exalt its outflowing operation.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 하늘 아래 모든 것을 낳은 도는 만물의 어머니라 할 수 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: (The Tao) which originated all under the sky is to be considered as the mother of them all.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 내가 큰 도에 따라 나라를 다스릴 기회를 얻는다면 가장 경계할 것은 잘난 체하며 뽐내는 일이다.
quotes.text_source_en: If I were suddenly to become known, and (put into a position to) conduct (a government) according to the Great Tao, what I should be most afraid of would be a boastful display.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 도에 능한 사람이 심은 것은 뽑히지 않고, 그가 품은 것은 빼앗기지 않는다. 그 덕은 자손에게 이어져 오래도록 제사를 받는다.
quotes.text_source_en: What (Tao's) skilful planter plants Can never be uptorn; What his skilful arms enfold, From him can ne'er be borne. Sons shall bring in lengthening line, Sacrifices to his shrine.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 덕을 두텁게 지닌 사람은 갓난아이와 같다. 독충도 쏘지 않고, 사나운 짐승도 덮치지 않으며, 맹금도 채가지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: He who has in himself abundantly the attributes (of the Tao) is like an infant. Poisonous insects will not sting him; fierce beasts will not seize him; birds of prey will not strike him.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 아는 사람은 말하지 않고, 말하기 좋아하는 사람은 알지 못한다.
quotes.text_source_en: He who knows (the Tao) does not (care to) speak (about it); he who is (ever ready to) speak about it does not know it.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 나라는 바른 원칙으로 다스리고 전쟁은 변화무쌍한 책략으로 치르지만, 세상을 얻는 것은 억지로 개입하지 않는 데서 이루어진다.
quotes.text_source_en: A state may be ruled by (measures of) correction; weapons of war may be used with crafty dexterity; (but) the kingdom is made one's own (only) by freedom from action and purpose.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 통치가 느슨해 보일 때 백성은 순박해지고, 통치가 지나치게 세밀하면 백성은 교활해진다. 불행 곁에 행복이 있고 행복 아래에 불행이 숨어 있으니 그 끝을 누가 알겠는가.
quotes.text_source_en: The government that seems the most unwise, Oft goodness to the people best supplies; That which is meddling, touching everything, Will work but ill, and disappointment bring. Misery!--happiness is to be found by its side! Happiness!--misery lurks beneath it! Who knows what either will come to in the end?
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 사람을 다스리고 하늘의 이치에 봉사하는 데는 절제보다 나은 것이 없다.
quotes.text_source_en: For regulating the human (in our constitution) and rendering the (proper) service to the heavenly, there is nothing like moderation.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 큰 나라를 다스리는 일은 작은 생선을 조리하는 것과 같다.
quotes.text_source_en: Governing a great state is like cooking small fish.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 큰 나라는 낮은 곳으로 흐르는 강과 같아야 한다. 낮은 자리에 있기에 세상의 작은 나라들이 모여드는 중심이 된다.
quotes.text_source_en: What makes a great state is its being (like) a low-lying, down-flowing (stream);--it becomes the centre to which tend (all the small states) under heaven.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 도는 만물 가운데 가장 귀한 자리다. 선한 사람에게는 보배가 되고, 선하지 못한 사람도 버리지 않고 지켜 준다.
quotes.text_source_en: Tao has of all things the most honoured place. No treasures give good men so rich a grace; Bad men it guards, and doth their ill efface.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 억지로 행동하지 말고, 일을 짐처럼 여기지 말며, 맛없는 것에서도 맛을 보라. 작은 것을 크게 여기고 적은 것을 많게 보며, 원한에는 덕으로 갚아라.
quotes.text_source_en: (It is the way of the Tao) to act without (thinking of) acting; to conduct affairs without (feeling the) trouble of them; to taste without discerning any flavour; to consider what is small as great, and a few as many; and to recompense injury with kindness.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 안정된 것은 붙잡기 쉽고, 조짐이 나타나기 전에는 대비하기 쉽다. 일은 생기기 전에 처리하고 혼란은 시작되기 전에 다스려야 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: That which is at rest is easily kept hold of; before a thing has given indications of its presence, it is easy to take measures against it; that which is brittle is easily broken; that which is very small is easily dispersed. Action should be taken before a thing has made its appearance; order should be secured before disorder has begun.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 옛날 도를 잘 실천한 사람들은 백성을 영리하게 만들려 하지 않고 오히려 소박하게 지키려 했다.
quotes.text_source_en: The ancients who showed their skill in practising the Tao did so, not to enlighten the people, but rather to make them simple and ignorant.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 강과 바다가 모든 골짜기의 물을 받아들이는 까닭은 자신을 더 낮게 두기 때문이다. 성인도 사람 위에 서려면 말로 자신을 낮추고, 앞에 서려면 몸을 뒤에 둔다.
quotes.text_source_en: That whereby the rivers and seas are able to receive the homage and tribute of all the valley streams, is their skill in being lower than they;--it is thus that they are the kings of them all. So it is that the sage (ruler), wishing to be above men, puts himself by his words below them, and, wishing to be before them, places his person behind them.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 세상은 나의 도가 크면서도 다른 가르침보다 못나 보인다고 말한다. 그러나 바로 그 크기 때문에 닮은 것이 없고, 무엇과 비슷했다면 진작 작아졌을 것이다.
quotes.text_source_en: All the world says that, while my Tao is great, it yet appears to be inferior (to other systems of teaching). Now it is just its greatness that makes it seem to be inferior. If it were like any other (system), for long would its smallness have been known!
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 싸움에 능한 사람은 사납게 보이지 않고, 잘 싸우는 사람은 분노하지 않으며, 잘 이기는 사람은 적과 무리하게 맞서지 않는다. 다투지 않는 데 참된 힘이 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: He who in (Tao's) wars has skill Assumes no martial port; He who fights with most good will To rage makes no resort. He who vanquishes yet still Keeps from his foes apart; He whose hests men most fulfil Yet humbly plies his art. Thus we say, 'He ne'er contends, And therein is his might.' Thus we say, 'Men's wills he bends, That they with him unite.' Thus we say, 'Like Heaven's his ends, No sage of old more bright.'
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 병법에 능한 사람은 먼저 공격하는 주인이 되기보다 방어하는 손님이 되기를 택하고, 한 치 나아가기보다 한 자 물러서기를 택한다.
quotes.text_source_en: A master of the art of war has said, 'I do not dare to be the host (to commence the war); I prefer to be the guest (to act on the defensive). I do not dare to advance an inch; I prefer to retire a foot.' This is called marshalling the ranks where there are no ranks; baring the arms (to fight) where there are no arms to bare; grasping the weapon where there is no weapon to grasp; advancing against the enemy where there is no enemy.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 내 말은 알기 쉽고 실천하기도 쉽지만, 세상에는 그것을 제대로 알고 실천하는 사람이 드물다.
quotes.text_source_en: My words are very easy to know, and very easy to practise; but there is no one in the world who is able to know and able to practise them.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 알면서도 모른다고 여기는 것이 가장 높고, 모르면서 안다고 여기는 것은 병이다.
quotes.text_source_en: To know and yet (think) we do not know is the highest (attainment); not to know (and yet think) we do know is a disease.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 사람들이 마땅히 두려워할 것을 두려워하지 않으면 더 큰 두려움이 닥친다.
quotes.text_source_en: When the people do not fear what they ought to fear, that which is their great dread will come on them.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 무모하게 대담한 사람은 죽고, 감히 함부로 하지 않는 사람은 산다. 어느 것이 이롭고 해로운지 하늘의 뜻은 쉽게 헤아릴 수 없다.
quotes.text_source_en: He whose boldness appears in his daring (to do wrong, in defiance of the laws) is put to death; he whose boldness appears in his not daring (to do so) lives on. Of these two cases the one appears to be advantageous, and the other to be injurious. But When Heaven's anger smites a man, Who the cause shall truly scan? On this account the sage feels a difficulty (as to what to do in the former case).
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 백성이 죽음을 두려워하지 않는다면 죽음으로 위협해 무엇을 이루겠는가.
quotes.text_source_en: The people do not fear death; to what purpose is it to (try to) frighten them with death? If the people were always in awe of death, and I could always seize those who do wrong, and put them to death, who would dare to do wrong?
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 백성이 굶주리는 것은 윗사람이 세금을 지나치게 거두기 때문이다.
quotes.text_source_en: The people suffer from famine because of the multitude of taxes consumed by their superiors. It is through this that they suffer famine.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 사람은 태어날 때 부드럽고 약하지만 죽을 때는 굳고 강하다. 풀과 나무도 살아 있을 때는 부드럽고 연하지만 죽으면 말라 굳는다.
quotes.text_source_en: Man at his birth is supple and weak; at his death, firm and strong. (So it is with) all things. Trees and plants, in their early growth, are soft and brittle; at their death, dry and withered.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 하늘의 도는 활을 당기는 것과 같다. 높은 곳은 낮추고 낮은 곳은 높이며, 넘치는 곳은 덜어 모자란 곳에 보탠다.
quotes.text_source_en: May not the Way (or Tao) of Heaven be compared to the (method of) bending a bow? The (part of the bow) which was high is brought low, and what was low is raised up. (So Heaven) diminishes where there is superabundance, and supplements where there is deficiency.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 세상에 물보다 부드럽고 약한 것은 없지만, 단단하고 강한 것을 공격하는 데 물보다 나은 것은 없다.
quotes.text_source_en: There is nothing in the world more soft and weak than water, and yet for attacking things that are firm and strong there is nothing that can take precedence of it;--for there is nothing (so effectual) for which it can be changed.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 큰 원한을 화해시켜도 마음에는 반드시 앙금이 남는다. 그것을 어찌 완전한 선이라 할 수 있겠는가.
quotes.text_source_en: When a reconciliation is effected (between two parties) after a great animosity, there is sure to be a grudge remaining (in the mind of the one who was wrong). And how can this be beneficial (to the other)?
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 작은 나라에 적은 백성이 살게 하고, 뛰어난 능력을 지닌 사람이 있어도 과하게 쓰지 않으며, 사람들이 죽음을 중히 여겨 함부로 먼 곳으로 떠나지 않게 하라.
quotes.text_source_en: In a little state with a small population, I would so order it, that, though there were individuals with the abilities of ten or a hundred men, there should be no employment of them; I would make the people, while looking on death as a grievous thing, yet not remove elsewhere (to avoid it).
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 진실한 말은 화려하지 않고 화려한 말은 진실하지 않다. 도에 능한 사람은 다투지 않고, 많이 안다고 뽐내는 사람은 참으로 알지 못한다.
quotes.text_source_en: Sincere words are not fine; fine words are not sincere. Those who are skilled (in the Tao) do not dispute (about it); the disputatious are not skilled in it. Those who know (the Tao) are not extensively learned; the extensively learned do not know it.
quotes.author: Laozi
quotes.work: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 젊은이는 집에서는 부모에게 효도하고, 밖에서는 어른을 공경해야 한다. 신중하고 믿음직하며, 널리 사람을 사랑하고 어진 이를 가까이해야 한다. 이를 행하고도 여력이 있으면 글과 예를 배워야 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: A youth, when at home, should be filial, and, abroad, respectful to his elders. He should be earnest and truthful. He should overflow in love to all, and cultivate the friendship of the good. When he has time and opportunity, after the performance of these things, he should employ them in polite studies.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 배우는 사람이 무게가 없으면 존경을 얻지 못하고, 그 배움도 견고하지 못하다.
quotes.text_source_en: The Master said, 'If the scholar be not grave, he will not call forth any veneration, and his learning will not be solid.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 자금이 자공에게 물었다. ‘선생님은 어느 나라에 가시든 그 정치 사정을 모두 아신다. 직접 물으시는가, 아니면 사람들이 알려 드리는가?’
quotes.text_source_en: Tsze-ch'in asked Tsze-kung, saying, 'When our master comes to any country, he does not fail to learn all about its government. Does he ask his information? or is it given to him?
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 아버지가 살아 계실 때에는 그 뜻을 살피고, 돌아가신 뒤에는 그 행실을 살펴라. 삼 년 동안 아버지의 도를 바꾸지 않는다면 효자라 할 수 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: While a man's father is alive, look at the bent of his will; when his father is dead, look at his conduct. If for three years he does not alter from the way of his father, he may be called filial.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 약속이 의로움에 맞으면 그 말을 실천할 수 있고, 공경이 예에 맞으면 치욕을 멀리할 수 있다. 의지하는 이가 가까이할 만한 사람이라면 그를 스승으로 삼을 수 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: When agreements are made according to what is right, what is spoken can be made good. When respect is shown according to what is proper, one keeps far from shame and disgrace. When the parties upon whom a man leans are proper persons to be intimate with, he can make them his guides and masters.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 덕으로 정치를 하는 이는 북극성과 같다. 자신은 제자리를 지키고, 뭇별이 그를 향한다.
quotes.text_source_en: He who exercises government by means of his virtue may be compared to the north polar star, which keeps its place and all the stars turn towards it.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 옛것을 익히면서 새것을 알아 가는 사람은 남의 스승이 될 수 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: If a man keeps cherishing his old knowledge, so as continually to be acquiring new, he may be a teacher of others.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 군자는 두루 어울리되 편당하지 않고, 소인은 편당하되 두루 어울리지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: The superior man is catholic and no partisan. The mean man is partisan and not catholic.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 곧은 사람을 등용하고 굽은 사람을 물리치면 백성이 따른다. 굽은 사람을 등용하고 곧은 사람을 물리치면 백성이 따르지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: Advance the upright and set aside the crooked, then the people will submit. Advance the crooked and set aside the upright, then the people will not submit.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 신의가 없는 사람이 어떻게 세상에 설 수 있는지 모르겠다. 큰 수레에 멍에걸이가 없고 작은 수레에 고삐걸이가 없다면 어떻게 나아가겠는가.
quotes.text_source_en: I do not know how a man without truthfulness is to get on. How can a large carriage be made to go without the cross-bar for yoking the oxen to, or a small carriage without the arrangement for yoking the horses?
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 사람다움이 없다면 예를 어디에 쓰겠는가. 사람다움이 없다면 음악을 어디에 쓰겠는가.
quotes.text_source_en: If a man be without the virtues proper to humanity, what has he to do with the rites of propriety? If a man be without the virtues proper to humanity, what has he to do with music?
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 태묘에 들어가 모든 일을 물은 것이 바로 예다.
quotes.text_source_en: Who will say that the son of the man of Tsau knows the rules of propriety! He has entered the grand temple and asks about everything.' The Master heard the remark, and said, 'This is a rule of propriety.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 그대들은 어찌 선생이 벼슬을 잃은 것을 걱정하는가. 천하에 도가 사라진 지 오래되었으니, 하늘이 그를 세상을 깨우는 목탁으로 삼으려는 것이다.
quotes.text_source_en: My friends, why are you distressed by your master's loss of office? The kingdom has long been without the principles of truth and right; Heaven is going to use your master as a bell with its wooden tongue.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 소악은 지극히 아름답고 또한 지극히 선하며, 무악은 지극히 아름답지만 지극히 선하지는 않다.
quotes.text_source_en: The Master said of the Shao that it was perfectly beautiful and also perfectly good. He said of the Wu that it was perfectly beautiful but not perfectly good.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 높은 자리에 있으면서 너그럽지 않고, 예를 행하면서 공경하지 않으며, 상을 치르면서 슬퍼하지 않는다면 무엇을 볼 만하겠는가.
quotes.text_source_en: High station filled without indulgent generosity; ceremonies performed without reverence; mourning conducted without sorrow;-- wherewith should I contemplate such ways?
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 어진 풍속이 있는 마을이 좋은 곳이다. 살 곳을 고르면서 어진 풍속이 있는 곳을 택하지 않는다면 어찌 지혜롭다 하겠는가.
quotes.text_source_en: It is virtuous manners which constitute the excellence of a neighborhood. If a man in selecting a residence, do not fix on one where such prevail, how can he be wise?
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 군자는 세상일에 무조건 찬성하거나 반대하지 않고, 오직 의로운 것을 따른다.
quotes.text_source_en: The superior man, in the world, does not set his mind either for anything, or against anything; what is right he will follow.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 군자는 덕을 생각하고 소인은 편안함을 생각한다. 군자는 법도를 생각하고 소인은 받을 혜택을 생각한다.
quotes.text_source_en: The superior man thinks of virtue; the small man thinks of comfort. The superior man thinks of the sanctions of law; the small man thinks of favours which he may receive.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 군자는 의로움에 밝고, 소인은 이익에 밝다.
quotes.text_source_en: The mind of the superior man is conversant with righteousness; the mind of the mean man is conversant with gain.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 군자는 말은 더디게 하고 행동은 민첩하게 하려 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: The superior man wishes to be slow in his speech and earnest in his conduct.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 자천은 참으로 덕이 높은 사람이다. 노나라에 어진 이들이 없었다면 그가 어떻게 그런 품성을 갖추었겠는가.
quotes.text_source_en: The Master said of Tsze-chien, 'Of superior virtue indeed is such a man! If there were not virtuous men in Lu, how could this man have acquired this character?
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 자산에게는 군자의 네 가지 덕이 있었다. 몸가짐은 겸손했고, 윗사람을 섬길 때는 공경했으며, 백성을 기를 때는 은혜로웠고, 백성을 다스릴 때는 공정했다.
quotes.text_source_en: The Master said of Tsze-ch'an that he had four of the characteristics of a superior man:-- in his conduct of himself, he was humble; in serving his superiors, he was respectful; in nourishing the people, he was kind; in ordering the people, he was just.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 나라가 잘 다스려질 때 영무자는 지혜롭게 처신했고, 나라가 어지러울 때는 어리석은 듯 처신했다. 그의 지혜는 따라갈 수 있어도 그 어리석은 듯함은 따라가기 어렵다.
quotes.text_source_en: When good order prevailed in his country, Ning Wu acted the part of a wise man. When his country was in disorder, he acted the part of a stupid man. Others may equal his wisdom, but they cannot equal his stupidity.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 미생고를 어찌 정직하다 하겠는가. 누가 식초를 빌리러 오자 이웃에게 빌려다가 주었다.
quotes.text_source_en: Who says of Wei-shang Kao that he is upright? One begged some vinegar of him, and he begged it of a neighbor and gave it to the man.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 교묘한 말과 아첨하는 얼굴, 지나친 공손은 좌구명이 부끄러워했고 나도 부끄러워한다. 원한을 숨기고 친한 체하는 일도 그가 부끄러워했고 나도 부끄러워한다.
quotes.text_source_en: Fine words, an insinuating appearance, and excessive respect;-- Tso Ch'iu-ming was ashamed of them. I also am ashamed of them. To conceal resentment against a person, and appear friendly with him;-- Tso Ch'iu-ming was ashamed of such conduct. I also am ashamed of it.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 너는 군자다운 선비가 되어라. 소인 같은 선비가 되지 마라.
quotes.text_source_en: The Master said to Tsze-hsia, 'Do you be a scholar after the style of the superior man, and not after that of the mean man.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 바탕이 문채보다 지나치면 거칠고, 문채가 바탕보다 지나치면 겉치레가 된다. 바탕과 문채가 고르게 어우러져야 군자다.
quotes.text_source_en: Where the solid qualities are in excess of accomplishments, we have rusticity; where the accomplishments are in excess of the solid qualities, we have the manners of a clerk. When the accomplishments and solid qualities are equally blended, we then have the man of virtue.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 사람은 곧게 태어난다. 곧음을 잃고도 살아남는다면 그것은 요행일 뿐이다.
quotes.text_source_en: Man is born for uprightness. If a man lose his uprightness, and yet live, his escape from death is the effect of mere good fortune.
quotes.author: Confucius and disciples (traditional compilation)

quotes.text_ko: 황색 가사를 걸쳤어도 품행이 나쁘고 절제하지 못하는 사람이 많다. 그런 악인은 자신의 악행으로 지옥에 간다.
quotes.text_source_en: Many men whose shoulders are covered with the yellow gown are ill-conditioned and unrestrained; such evil-doers by their evil deeds go to hell.

quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 악하고 절제하지 못한 사람이 나라의 보시로 사느니, 불타는 뜨거운 쇠구슬을 삼키는 편이 낫다.
quotes.text_source_en: Better it would be to swallow a heated iron ball, like flaring fire, than that a bad unrestrained fellow should live on the charity of the land.

quotes.text_ko: 이웃의 아내를 탐하는 경솔한 사람은 네 가지를 얻는다. 나쁜 평판, 편치 않은 잠자리, 벌, 그리고 지옥이다.
quotes.text_source_en: Four things does a wreckless man gain who covets his neighbour's wife,--a bad reputation, an uncomfortable bed, thirdly, punishment, and lastly, hell.
quotes.author: Teachings attributed to the Buddha
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 해야 할 일이 있다면 힘차게 해내라. 게으른 수행은 욕망의 먼지만 더 널리 흩뿌린다.
quotes.text_source_en: If anything is to be done, let a man do it, let him attack it vigorously! A careless pilgrim only scatters the dust of his passions more widely.
quotes.author: Teachings attributed to the Buddha
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 악행은 하지 않는 것이 낫다. 뒤에 후회하기 때문이다. 선행은 하는 것이 낫다. 하고 나면 후회하지 않기 때문이다.
quotes.text_source_en: An evil deed is better left undone, for a man repents of it afterwards; a good deed is better done, for having done it, one does not repent.

quotes.text_ko: 길든 코끼리를 전쟁터로 이끌고 왕도 길든 코끼리를 탄다. 모욕을 말없이 견디는, 자신을 길들인 사람이 사람 가운데 으뜸이다.
quotes.text_source_en: They lead a tamed elephant to battle, the king mounts a tamed elephant; the tamed is the best among men, he who silently endures abuse.
quotes.author: Teachings attributed to the Buddha
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 어떤 짐승을 타도 사람이 가지 못한 열반에 이를 수는 없다. 자신을 잘 길들인 사람은 길든 자기 자신을 타고 그곳에 간다.
quotes.text_source_en: For with these animals does no man reach the untrodden country (Nirvana), where a tamed man goes on a tamed animal, viz. on his own well-tamed self.
quotes.author: Teachings attributed to the Buddha
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 많이 먹고 살찌며 잠만 자고 뒹구는 어리석은 이는 먹이를 먹고 자란 돼지처럼 거듭 태어난다.
quotes.text_source_en: If a man becomes fat and a great eater, if he is sleepy and rolls himself about, that fool, like a hog fed on wash, is born again and again.

quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 분별 있고 지혜로우며 절제해 함께 걷는 벗을 찾으면, 사려 깊고 기쁘게 그와 동행하며 모든 위험을 이겨 내라.
quotes.text_source_en: If a man find a prudent companion who walks with him, is wise, and lives soberly, he may walk with him, overcoming all dangers, happy, but considerate.

quotes.text_ko: 세상에서 어머니의 지위는 즐겁고 아버지의 지위도 즐겁다. 수행자의 삶도 즐겁고 성자의 삶도 즐겁다.
quotes.text_source_en: Pleasant in the world is the state of a mother, pleasant the state of a father, pleasant the state of a Samana, pleasant the state of a Brahmana.

quotes.text_source_en: He who overcomes this fierce thirst, difficult to be conquered in this world, sufferings fall off from him, like water-drops from a lotus leaf.

quotes.text_source_en: The channels run everywhere, the creeper (of passion) stands sprouting; if you see the creeper springing up, cut its root by means of knowledge.

quotes.text_source_en: A creature's pleasures are extravagant and luxurious; sunk in lust and looking for pleasure, men undergo (again and again) birth and decay.

quotes.text_source_en: Men, driven on by thirst, run about like a snared hare; let therefore the mendicant drive out thirst, by striving after passionlessness for himself.

quotes.text_source_en: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by vanity: therefore a gift bestowed on those who are free from vanity brings great reward.

quotes.text_ko: 법 안에 살고 법을 기뻐하며 법을 명상하고 법을 따르는 수행자는 참된 법에서 벗어나지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: He who dwells in the law, delights in the law, meditates on the law, follows the law, that Bhikshu will never fall away from the true law.

quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_source_en: Without knowledge there is no meditation, without meditation there is no knowledge: he who has knowledge and meditation is near unto Nirvana.

quotes.text_ko: 몸과 말과 마음이 고요하고 정신이 모이며 세상의 미끼를 버린 수행자를 고요한 이라 부른다.
quotes.text_source_en: The Bhikshu whose body and tongue and mind are quieted, who is collected, and has rejected the baits of the world, he is called quiet.

quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 기쁨이 충만하고 붓다의 가르침 안에서 고요한 수행자는 욕망이 멎는 평온한 곳, 열반의 행복에 이른다.
quotes.text_source_en: The Bhikshu, full of delight, who is calm in the doctrine of Buddha will reach the quiet place (Nirvana), cessation of natural desires, and happiness.
quotes.author: Teachings attributed to the Buddha
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 절제와 명상이라는 두 법에서 저편 기슭에 이른 바라문에게는 지식을 얻는 순간 모든 속박이 사라진다.
quotes.text_source_en: If the Brahmana has reached the other shore in both laws (in restraint and contemplation), all bonds vanish from him who has obtained knowledge.
quotes.author: Teachings attributed to the Buddha
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 삶의 쾌락에서 마음을 거두는 것은 바라문에게 큰 이익이다. 해치려는 뜻이 모두 사라지면 고통도 멎는다.
quotes.text_source_en: It advantages a Brahmana not a little if he holds his mind back from the pleasures of life; when all wish to injure has vanished, pain will cease.

quotes.text_ko: 끈과 고삐와 사슬과 그에 딸린 모든 것을 끊고 문빗장을 부수어 깨어난 이를 나는 참된 바라문이라 부른다.
quotes.text_source_en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has cut the strap and the thong, the chain with all that pertains to it, who has burst the bar, and is awakened.
quotes.author: Teachings attributed to the Buddha
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 이 세상에서 선과 악, 그 둘의 속박을 넘어 슬픔과 죄와 더러움에서 벗어난 이를 나는 참된 바라문이라 부른다.
quotes.text_source_en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who in this world is above good and evil, above the bondage of both, free from grief from sin, and from impurity.
quotes.author: Teachings attributed to the Buddha

quotes.text_ko: 앞이나 뒤나 그 사이의 어떤 것도 자기 것이라 하지 않고, 소유 없이 세상에 대한 애착에서 벗어난 이를 나는 참된 바라문이라 부른다.
quotes.text_source_en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who calls nothing his own, whether it be before, behind, or between, who is poor, and free from the love of the world.
quotes.author: Teachings attributed to the Buddha
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 우리의 힘으로 할 수 있는 일이 있고, 우리의 힘을 넘어서는 일이 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: There are things which are within our power, and there are things which are beyond our power.
