quotes.text_ko: 욕망은 원하는 것을 얻으려 하고 혐오는 싫어하는 것을 피하려 한다. 원하는 것을 얻지 못하면 실망하고, 피하려던 일을 만나면 비참해진다는 것을 기억하라.
quotes.text_source_en: Remember that desire demands the attainment of that of which you are desirous; and aversion demands the avoidance of that to which you are averse; that he who fails of the object of his desires is disappointed; and he who incurs the object of his aversion is wretched.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 마음을 기쁘게 하거나 쓸모 있거나 사랑하는 대상이 어떤 본성을 지녔는지 늘 떠올려라. 좋아하는 잔은 그저 하나의 잔이고, 안고 있는 아이와 배우자는 죽을 수 있는 존재임을 기억하면 잃음도 견딜 수 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: With regard to whatever objects either delight the mind or contribute to use or are tenderly beloved, remind yourself of what nature they are, beginning with the merest trifles: if you have a favorite cup, that it is but a cup of which you are fond of—for thus, if it is broken, you can bear it; if you embrace your child or your wife, that you embrace a mortal—and thus, if either of them dies, you can bear it.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 어떤 행동을 시작할 때에는 먼저 그 행동이 어떤 성격의 일인지 생각하라.
quotes.text_source_en: When you set about any action, remind yourself of what nature the action is.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 사람을 괴롭히는 것은 사물 자체가 아니라 사물에 대한 그의 판단이다.
quotes.text_source_en: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 자신의 것이 아닌 뛰어남 때문에 우쭐하지 마라.
quotes.text_source_en: Be not elated at any excellence not your own.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 배가 정박했을 때 물을 구하러 내려 조개나 버섯을 줍더라도 생각은 늘 배를 향해야 한다. 선장이 부르면 모든 것을 두고 즉시 돌아가야 한다. 삶의 배우자와 자녀도 이와 같다.
quotes.text_source_en: As in a voyage, when the ship is at anchor, if you go on shore to get water, you may amuse yourself with picking up a shellfish or a truffle in your way, but your thoughts ought to be bent toward the ship, and perpetually attentive, lest the captain should call, and then you must leave all these things, that you may not have to be carried on board the vessel, bound like a sheep; thus likewise in life, if, instead of a truffle or shellfish, such a thing as a wife or a child be granted you, there is no objection; but if the captain calls, run to the ship, leave all these things, and never look behind.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 일이 네 뜻대로 일어나기를 요구하지 말고, 일어나는 대로 일어나기를 바라라. 그러면 삶이 순조로울 것이다.
quotes.text_source_en: Demand not that events should happen as you wish; but wish them to happen as they do happen, and you will go on well.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 질병은 몸을 방해하지만, 의지가 스스로 허락하지 않는 한 의지를 방해하지는 못한다.
quotes.text_source_en: Sickness is an impediment to the body, but not to the will unless itself pleases.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 어떤 일이 닥치든 자신에게로 돌아가, 그것을 활용할 어떤 능력이 내게 있는지 물어라.
quotes.text_source_en: Upon every accident, remember to turn toward yourself and inquire what faculty you have for its use.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 어떤 것에 대해서도 ‘잃었다’고 말하지 말고 ‘돌려주었다’고 말하라.
quotes.text_source_en: Never say of anything, “I have lost it,” but, “I have restored it.” Has your child died?
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 나아지고 싶다면 ‘일을 돌보지 않으면 생계를 잃는다’ 같은 계산을 버려라. 근심과 두려움 속에서 풍족하게 사느니 그것들에서 벗어나 굶어 죽는 편이 낫다.
quotes.text_source_en: If you would improve, lay aside such reasonings as these: “If I neglect my affairs, I shall not have a maintenance; if I do not punish my servant, he will be good for nothing.” For it were better to die of hunger, exempt from grief and fear, than to live in affluence with perturbation; and it is better that your servant should be bad than you unhappy.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 나아지고 싶다면 외적인 일에 관해 어리석고 둔하다는 평을 받는 데 만족하라.
quotes.text_source_en: If you would improve, be content to be thought foolish and dull with regard to externals.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 자녀와 배우자와 친구가 영원히 살기를 바란다면 어리석다. 네 힘 밖의 일을 네 힘 안에 두고, 남의 것을 네 것으로 만들려 하기 때문이다.
quotes.text_source_en: If you wish your children and your wife and your friends to live forever, you are foolish, for you wish things to be in your power which are not so, and what belongs to others to be your own.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 잔치에 참석한 사람처럼 행동해야 한다는 것을 기억하라.
quotes.text_source_en: Remember that you must behave as at a banquet.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 누군가 슬퍼하며 우는 것을 보아도 겉으로 드러난 불행에 압도되지 마라. 그를 아프게 하는 것은 사건 자체가 아니라 그 사건에 대한 판단임을 분별하라. 다만 대화할 때에는 그와 공감하고 필요하면 함께 탄식하라.
quotes.text_source_en: When you see anyone weeping for grief, either that his son has gone abroad or that he has suffered in his affairs, take care not to be overcome by the apparent evil, but discriminate and be ready to say, “What hurts this man is not this occurrence itself—for another man might not be hurt by it—but the view he chooses to take of it.” As far as conversation goes, however, do not disdain to accommodate yourself to him and, if need be, to groan with him.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 너는 작가가 정한 극에서 맡은 역할을 연기하는 배우임을 기억하라. 짧은 극이면 짧게, 긴 극이면 길게 연기해야 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: Remember that you are an actor in a drama of such sort as the Author chooses—if short, then in a short one; if long, then in a long one.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 까마귀가 불길하게 울어도 겉모습에 압도되지 말고 분별하라. 그것은 내 보잘것없는 몸이나 재산, 평판, 자녀나 배우자에게 닥칠 일을 예고하지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: When a raven happens to croak unluckily, be not overcome by appearances, but discriminate and say, “Nothing is portended to me, either to my paltry body, or property, or reputation, or children, or wife.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 이길 수 있는지가 자신의 힘에 달리지 않은 싸움에는 들어가지 않으면, 누구에게도 정복당하지 않을 수 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: You can be unconquerable if you enter into no combat in which it is not in your own power to conquer.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 모욕하거나 때린 사람이 우리를 모욕하는 것이 아니라, 그 일을 모욕으로 판단하는 우리의 생각이 우리를 모욕한다.
quotes.text_source_en: Remember that it is not he who gives abuse or blows, who affronts, but the view we take of these things as insulting.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 죽음과 추방을 비롯해 두려워 보이는 모든 것을 날마다 눈앞에 두라. 특히 죽음을 생각하면 비굴한 생각도 지나친 욕망도 품지 않게 된다.
quotes.text_source_en: Let death and exile, and all other things which appear terrible, be daily before your eyes, but death chiefly; and you will never entertain an abject thought, nor too eagerly covet anything.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 철학을 진지하게 원한다면 처음부터 사람들이 비웃고 조롱할 준비를 하라. 교만한 표정을 짓지 말고, 신이 맡긴 자리처럼 자신이 가장 옳다고 여기는 것에 굳게 머물러라.
quotes.text_source_en: If you have an earnest desire toward philosophy, prepare yourself from the very first to have the multitude laugh and sneer, and say, “He is returned to us a philosopher all at once”; and, “Whence this supercilious look?” Now, for your part, do not have a supercilious look indeed, but keep steadily to those things which appear best to you, as one appointed by God to this particular station.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 누군가를 기쁘게 하려고 외적인 것에 마음을 돌리는 순간, 자신의 삶의 계획을 망쳤음을 알아라.
quotes.text_source_en: If you ever happen to turn your attention to externals, for the pleasure of anyone, be assured that you have ruined your scheme of life.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: ‘평판을 잃고 어디서도 아무것도 아닌 사람이 될 것이다’라는 생각으로 괴로워하지 마라. 불명예가 악이라면 남이 너를 악에 빠뜨릴 수는 없다.
quotes.text_source_en: Let not such considerations as these distress you: “I shall live in discredit and be nobody anywhere.” For if discredit be an evil, you can no more be involved in evil through another than in baseness.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 잔치나 호의나 친밀한 관계에서 누군가가 너보다 우선 대접받는가.
quotes.text_source_en: Is anyone preferred before you at an entertainment, or in courtesies, or in confidential intercourse?
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 자연의 뜻은 우리 모두가 동의하는 일들을 통해 배울 수 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: The will of nature may be learned from things upon which we are all agreed.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 표적이 빗나가도록 세워진 것이 아니듯, 악의 본성도 세상에 목적처럼 세워진 것은 아니다.
quotes.text_source_en: As a mark is not set up for the sake of missing the aim, so neither does the nature of evil exist in the world.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 누군가 네 몸을 지나가는 사람에게 넘겨주었다면 분명 화를 낼 것이다.
quotes.text_source_en: If a person had delivered up your body to some passer-by, you would certainly be angry.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 의무는 언제나 관계에 따라 정해진다.
quotes.text_source_en: Duties are universally measured by relations.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 신에 대한 경건의 핵심은 그들이 존재하며 우주를 정의롭고 선하게 다스린다는 올바른 생각을 갖는 데 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: Be assured that the essence of piety toward the gods lies in this—to form right opinions concerning them, as existing and as governing the universe justly and well.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 점술가를 찾을 때에는 결과가 무엇인지 몰라 배우러 간다는 사실을 기억하라. 그러나 철학적이라면 그 결과가 선인지 악인지는 이미 알고 있어야 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: When you have recourse to divination, remember that you know not what the event will be, and you come to learn it of the diviner; but of what nature it is you knew before coming; at least, if you are of philosophic mind.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 혼자 있을 때나 사람들과 함께 있을 때나 지킬 수 있는 성품과 태도를 먼저 자신에게 정해 두어라.
quotes.text_source_en: Begin by prescribing to yourself some character and demeanor, such as you may preserve both alone and in company.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 약속된 쾌락의 겉모습에 눈이 부시면 그것에 휩쓸리지 않도록 경계하라. 일을 잠시 미루고 스스로에게 생각할 시간을 주어라.
quotes.text_source_en: If you are dazzled by the semblance of any promised pleasure, guard yourself against being bewildered by it; but let the affair wait your leisure, and procure yourself some delay.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 분명한 판단으로 옳다고 여겨 행동했다면 세상이 오해하더라도 그 행동이 보이는 것을 두려워하지 마라. 옳지 않다면 행동 자체를 피하고, 옳다면 잘못 비난하는 사람을 왜 두려워하는가.
quotes.text_source_en: When you do anything from a clear judgment that it ought to be done, never shrink from being seen to do it, even though the world should misunderstand it; for if you are not acting rightly, shun the action itself; if you are, why fear those who wrongly censure you?
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: ‘낮이거나 밤이다’라는 말은 양자택일 논증에서는 강하지만 둘을 함께 묶는 논증에서는 쓸모없다. 잔치에서 가장 큰 몫을 고르는 것도 몸의 욕구에는 맞지만 함께하는 정신에는 맞지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: As the proposition, “either it is day or it is night,” has much force in a disjunctive argument, but none at all in a conjunctive one, so, at a feast, to choose the largest share is very suitable to the bodily appetite, but utterly inconsistent with the social spirit of the entertainment.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 힘에 넘치는 역할을 맡으면 그 역할도 제대로 하지 못하고, 감당할 수 있었던 역할마저 버리게 된다.
quotes.text_source_en: If you have assumed any character beyond your strength, you have both demeaned yourself ill in that and quitted one which you might have supported.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 걸을 때 못을 밟거나 발목을 접질리지 않게 조심하듯, 마음을 다스리는 능력이 상하지 않도록 조심하라.
quotes.text_source_en: As in walking you take care not to tread upon a nail, or turn your foot, so likewise take care not to hurt the ruling faculty of your mind.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 신발의 크기가 발에 맞아야 하듯, 각자의 소유는 몸의 필요를 기준으로 해야 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: The body is to everyone the proper measure of its possessions, as the foot is of the shoe.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 열네 살 무렵의 여성들은 남자들에게 ‘여주인’이라는 아첨을 듣는다.
quotes.text_source_en: Women from fourteen years old are flattered by men with the title of mistresses.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 운동과 먹고 마시는 일과 몸의 기능에 지나치게 많은 시간을 쓰는 것은 지성이 부족하다는 표시다.
quotes.text_source_en: It is a mark of want of intellect to spend much time in things relating to the body, as to be immoderate in exercises, in eating and drinking, and in the discharge of other animal functions.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 누군가 네게 나쁘게 행동하거나 험담하면, 그는 그렇게 하는 것이 옳다고 여긴 판단에 따라 행동한다는 것을 기억하라.
quotes.text_source_en: When any person does ill by you, or speaks ill of you, remember that he acts or speaks from an impression that it is right for him to do so.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 모든 일에는 두 손잡이가 있다. 하나는 견딜 수 있게 하는 손잡이이고, 다른 하나는 견딜 수 없게 하는 손잡이다.
quotes.text_source_en: Everything has two handles: one by which it may be borne, another by which it cannot.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: ‘내가 더 부유하니 너보다 우월하다’거나 ‘내가 더 말을 잘하니 너보다 우월하다’는 추론은 성립하지 않는다. 재산과 말솜씨가 더 나을 뿐, 너 자신은 재산도 문체도 아니다.
quotes.text_source_en: These reasonings have no logical connection: “I am richer than you, therefore I am your superior.” “I am more eloquent than you, therefore I am your superior.” The true logical connection is rather this: “I am richer than you, therefore my possessions must exceed yours.” “I am more eloquent than you, therefore my style must surpass yours.” But you, after all, consist neither in property nor in style.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 누군가 급히 목욕한다고 해서 ‘나쁘게 한다’고 말하지 말고 ‘급히 한다’고 말하라.
quotes.text_source_en: Does anyone bathe hastily? Do not say that he does it ill, but hastily.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 스스로 철학자라고 선언하지 말고, 모르는 사람들 앞에서 원칙을 많이 말하지도 마라. 행동으로 보여 주어라.
quotes.text_source_en: Never proclaim yourself a philosopher, nor make much talk among the ignorant about your principles, but show them by actions.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 몸을 검소하게 먹이는 법을 배웠다고 자랑하지 마라. 물만 마신다고 매번 말하지도 마라. 가난한 이들이 우리보다 얼마나 검소하고 고난을 더 잘 견디는지 먼저 생각하라.
quotes.text_source_en: When you have learned to nourish your body frugally, do not pique yourself upon it; nor, if you drink water, be saying upon every occasion, “I drink water.” But first consider how much more frugal are the poor than we, and how much more patient of hardship.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 평범한 사람은 도움도 해로움도 자신에게서 찾지 않고 오직 외부에서만 찾는다.
quotes.text_source_en: The condition and characteristic of a vulgar person is that he never looks for either help or harm from himself, but only from externals.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 누군가 크리시포스의 글을 이해하고 해석한다며 뽐내면 이렇게 생각하라. ‘크리시포스가 어렵게 쓰지 않았다면 저 사람은 자랑할 것이 없었겠지.’
quotes.text_source_en: When anyone shows himself vain on being able to understand and interpret the works of Chrysippus, say to yourself: “Unless Chrysippus had written obscurely, this person would have had nothing to be vain of.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 채택한 원칙은 법처럼 지켜라. 그것을 어기는 일이 불경한 것처럼 여기고, 남이 너를 어떻게 말하는지는 신경 쓰지 마라. 그것은 네 일이 아니다.
quotes.text_source_en: Whatever rules you have adopted, abide by them as laws, and as if you would be impious to transgress them; and do not regard what anyone says of you, for this, after all, is no concern of yours.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 철학에서 첫째이자 가장 필요한 것은 ‘거짓말하지 말아야 한다’ 같은 원칙의 실천이다. 둘째는 왜 그래야 하는지의 증명이고, 셋째는 그 증명이 왜 성립하는지를 설명하는 논리다.
quotes.text_source_en: The first and most necessary topic in philosophy is the practical application of principles, as, We ought not to lie; the second is that of demonstrations as, Why it is that we ought not to lie; the third, that which gives strength and logical connection to the other two, as, Why this is a demonstration.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 지형에는 멀고 가까움, 험하고 안전함, 넓은 들과 좁은 길, 살고 죽을 가능성이 포함된다.
quotes.text_source_en: Earth comprises distances, great and small; danger and security; open ground and narrow passes; the chances of life and death.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 모든 장수는 이 다섯 요소를 익혀야 한다. 이를 아는 이는 이기고, 모르는 이는 패한다.
quotes.text_source_en: These five heads should be familiar to every general: he who knows them will be victorious; he who knows them not will fail.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 이 일곱 가지를 헤아리면 승리와 패배를 미리 알 수 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: By means of these seven considerations I can forecast victory or defeat.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 모든 전쟁은 속임수에 바탕을 둔다.
quotes.text_source_en: All warfare is based on deception.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 공격할 수 있을 때 공격하지 못하는 듯 보이고, 병력을 쓸 때 움직이지 않는 듯 보여라. 가까이 있을 때는 멀리 있는 듯, 멀리 있을 때는 가까이 있는 듯 믿게 하라.
quotes.text_source_en: Hence, when able to attack, we must seem unable; when using our forces, we must seem inactive; when we are near, we must make the enemy believe we are far away; when far away, we must make him believe we are near.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 적이 대비하지 않은 곳을 공격하고, 적이 예상하지 못한 곳에 나타나라.
quotes.text_source_en: Attack him where he is unprepared, appear where you are not expected.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 전쟁의 해로움을 철저히 아는 사람만이 전쟁을 이롭게 수행하는 법도 철저히 이해할 수 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: It is only one who is thoroughly acquainted with the evils of war that can thoroughly understand the profitable way of carrying it on.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 전쟁 물자는 본국에서 가져오되 식량은 적지에서 조달하라. 그러면 군대가 필요한 식량을 충분히 얻는다.
quotes.text_source_en: Bring war material with you from home, but forage on the enemy. Thus the army will have food enough for its needs.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 적을 죽이게 하려면 병사들의 분노를 일으켜야 하고, 적을 이긴 이익을 얻으려면 상을 주어야 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: Now in order to kill the enemy, our men must be roused to anger; that there may be advantage from defeating the enemy, they must have their rewards.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 전차전에서 열 대 이상을 빼앗으면 먼저 빼앗은 자에게 상을 주어라. 적의 깃발을 우리 깃발로 바꾸고 노획한 전차를 우리 것과 함께 쓰며, 포로는 친절히 대우해 보존하라.
quotes.text_source_en: Therefore in chariot fighting, when ten or more chariots have been taken, those should be rewarded who took the first. Our own flags should be substituted for those of the enemy, and the chariots mingled and used in conjunction with ours. The captured soldiers should be kindly treated and kept.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 전쟁의 큰 목적은 승리이지 오래 끄는 작전이 아니다.
quotes.text_source_en: In war, then, let your great object be victory, not lengthy campaigns.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 군대를 이끄는 이는 백성의 운명을 결정하며, 나라가 평안할지 위험할지가 그에게 달려 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: Thus it may be known that the leader of armies is the arbiter of the people’s fate, the man on whom it depends whether the nation shall be in peace or in peril.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 전쟁에서 가장 좋은 것은 적국을 온전히 보전한 채 얻는 것이며, 파괴하는 것은 그보다 못하다. 적의 군대와 부대도 온전히 사로잡는 것이 파괴하는 것보다 낫다.
quotes.text_source_en: Sun Tzŭ said: In the practical art of war, the best thing of all is to take the enemy’s country whole and intact; to shatter and destroy it is not so good. So, too, it is better to capture an army entire than to destroy it, to capture a regiment, a detachment or a company entire than to destroy them.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 최고의 용병은 적의 계획을 꺾는 것이고, 그다음은 적의 연합을 막는 것이며, 그다음은 야전군을 치는 것이다. 성을 포위하는 것은 가장 나쁜 방책이다.
quotes.text_source_en: Thus the highest form of generalship is to baulk the enemy’s plans; the next best is to prevent the junction of the enemy’s forces; the next in order is to attack the enemy’s army in the field; and the worst policy of all is to besiege walled cities.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 병력이 적의 열 배면 포위하고, 다섯 배면 공격하며, 두 배면 병력을 나누어 운용하는 것이 전쟁의 원칙이다.
quotes.text_source_en: It is the rule in war, if our forces are ten to the enemy’s one, to surround him; if five to one, to attack him; if twice as numerous, to divide our army into two.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 병력이 같으면 싸울 수 있고, 조금 열세면 피할 수 있으며, 모든 면에서 크게 열세면 물러나야 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: If equally matched, we can offer battle; if slightly inferior in numbers, we can avoid the enemy; if quite unequal in every way, we can flee from him.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 장수는 국가의 방벽이다. 방벽이 온전하면 나라가 강하고, 방벽에 결함이 있으면 나라가 약하다.
quotes.text_source_en: Now the general is the bulwark of the State: if the bulwark is complete at all points; the State will be strong; if the bulwark is defective, the State will be weak.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 적을 알고 자신을 알면 백 번 싸워도 위태롭지 않다. 자신만 알고 적을 모르면 한 번 이기고 한 번 진다. 적도 자신도 모르면 싸울 때마다 진다.
quotes.text_source_en: Hence the saying: If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles. If you know yourself but not the enemy, for every victory gained you will also suffer a defeat. If you know neither the enemy nor yourself, you will succumb in every battle.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 옛날의 뛰어난 전사들은 먼저 자신을 패할 수 없는 자리에 두고, 그다음 적을 이길 기회를 기다렸다.
quotes.text_source_en: Sun Tzŭ said: The good fighters of old first put themselves beyond the possibility of defeat, and then waited for an opportunity of defeating the enemy.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 패하지 않도록 하는 것은 우리 손에 달렸지만, 적을 이길 기회는 적이 제공한다.
quotes.text_source_en: To secure ourselves against defeat lies in our own hands, but the opportunity of defeating the enemy is provided by the enemy himself.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 뛰어난 전사는 자신이 패하지 않게 할 수는 있지만, 반드시 적을 이긴다고 보장할 수는 없다.
quotes.text_source_en: Thus the good fighter is able to secure himself against defeat, but cannot make certain of defeating the enemy.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 그는 실수하지 않음으로써 이긴다. 실수하지 않는다는 것은 이미 패한 적을 이기는 것이므로 승리를 확실하게 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: He wins his battles by making no mistakes. Making no mistakes is what establishes the certainty of victory, for it means conquering an enemy that is already defeated.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 능숙한 전사는 패배가 불가능한 위치에 자신을 두고, 적을 이길 순간을 놓치지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: Hence the skilful fighter puts himself into a position which makes defeat impossible, and does not miss the moment for defeating the enemy.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 승리하는 전략가는 먼저 이길 조건을 만든 뒤 싸움을 찾고, 패할 사람은 먼저 싸운 뒤 승리를 찾는다.
quotes.text_source_en: Thus it is that in war the victorious strategist only seeks battle after the victory has been won, whereas he who is destined to defeat first fights and afterwards looks for victory.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 전군이 적의 공격을 받아도 흔들리지 않게 하는 것은 정공과 기공의 운용에 달려 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: To ensure that your whole host may withstand the brunt of the enemy’s attack and remain unshaken—this is effected by manœuvers direct and indirect.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 군대의 충격을 숫돌로 달걀을 치는 것처럼 만드는 것은 강점과 약점을 아는 데 달려 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: That the impact of your army may be like a grindstone dashed against an egg—this is effected by the science of weak points and strong.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 싸움을 시작할 때는 정공을 쓰지만 승리를 얻으려면 기공이 필요하다.
quotes.text_source_en: In all fighting, the direct method may be used for joining battle, but indirect methods will be needed in order to secure victory.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 공격 방법은 정공과 기공 두 가지뿐이지만, 이 둘의 결합은 끝없는 변화로 이어진다.
quotes.text_source_en: In battle, there are not more than two methods of attack—the direct and the indirect; yet these two in combination give rise to an endless series of manœuvers.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 혼란을 가장하려면 완전한 규율이 있어야 하고, 두려움을 가장하려면 용기가 있어야 하며, 약함을 가장하려면 힘이 있어야 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: Simulated disorder postulates perfect discipline; simulated fear postulates courage; simulated weakness postulates strength.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 적을 잘 움직이는 사람은 거짓 모습을 보여 적이 그에 따라 행동하게 한다. 미끼를 내주어 적이 낚아채게 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: Thus one who is skilful at keeping the enemy on the move maintains deceitful appearances, according to which the enemy will act. He sacrifices something, that the enemy may snatch at it.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 상대가 무엇을 지켜야 할지 모르게 하는 장수는 공격에 능하고, 상대가 무엇을 공격해야 할지 모르게 하는 장수는 방어에 능하다.
quotes.text_source_en: Hence that general is skilful in attack whose opponent does not know what to defend; and he is skilful in defence whose opponent does not know what to attack.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 싸울 곳을 알려서는 안 된다. 그러면 적은 여러 지점에 대비하느라 병력을 분산하고, 우리가 한 지점에서 상대할 병력은 줄어든다.
quotes.text_source_en: The spot where we intend to fight must not be made known; for then the enemy will have to prepare against a possible attack at several different points; and his forces being thus distributed in many directions, the numbers we shall have to face at any given point will be proportionately few.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 적의 수가 더 많아도 싸우지 못하게 할 수 있다. 계책을 세워 적의 계획과 성공 가능성을 알아내라.
quotes.text_source_en: Though the enemy be stronger in numbers, we may prevent him from fighting. Scheme so as to discover his plans and the likelihood of their success.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 전쟁에서는 강한 곳을 피하고 약한 곳을 쳐야 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: So in war, the way is to avoid what is strong and to strike at what is weak.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 물이 흐르는 땅의 모양에 따라 길을 만들듯, 군대는 맞선 적에 따라 승리를 만들어 낸다.
quotes.text_source_en: Water shapes its course according to the nature of the ground over which it flows; the soldier works out his victory in relation to the foe whom he is facing.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 적을 다른 길로 유인해 멀고 굽은 길을 가면서도 늦게 출발해 먼저 목적지에 이르는 것이 우회의 계책을 아는 것이다.
quotes.text_source_en: Thus, to take a long and circuitous route, after enticing the enemy out of the way, and though starting after him, to contrive to reach the goal before him, shows knowledge of the artifice of deviation.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 강한 병사는 앞서고 지친 병사는 뒤처지므로, 이런 방식이면 군대의 십분의 일만 목적지에 이른다.
quotes.text_source_en: The stronger men will be in front, the jaded ones will fall behind, and on this plan only one-tenth of your army will reach its destination.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 규율 있고 침착하게 적에게 혼란과 소란이 생기기를 기다리는 것이 평정심을 지키는 기술이다.
quotes.text_source_en: Disciplined and calm, to await the appearance of disorder and hubbub amongst the enemy:—this is the art of retaining self-possession.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 깃발이 질서정연한 적을 가로막지 않고, 침착하고 자신 있게 진을 친 군대를 공격하지 않는 것이 형세를 살피는 기술이다.
quotes.text_source_en: To refrain from intercepting an enemy whose banners are in perfect order, to refrain from attacking an army drawn up in calm and confident array:—this is the art of studying circumstances.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 도망치는 척하는 적을 추격하지 말고, 사기가 날카로운 병사를 공격하지 마라.
quotes.text_source_en: Do not pursue an enemy who simulates flight; do not attack soldiers whose temper is keen.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 전쟁에서 장수는 군주의 명을 받고 군대를 모아 병력을 집중한다.
quotes.text_source_en: Sun Tzŭ said: In war, the general receives his commands from the sovereign, collects his army and concentrates his forces.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 전술을 바꾸는 데 따르는 이점을 철저히 이해하는 장수는 병력을 다룰 줄 안다.
quotes.text_source_en: The general who thoroughly understands the advantages that accompany variation of tactics knows how to handle his troops.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 이 이점을 이해하지 못한 장수는 지형을 잘 알아도 그 지식을 실제로 활용하지 못한다.
quotes.text_source_en: The general who does not understand these, may be well acquainted with the configuration of the country, yet he will not be able to turn his knowledge to practical account.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 계획을 변화시키는 기술을 모르는 전쟁 연구자는 다섯 가지 이점을 알아도 병력을 제대로 쓰지 못한다.
quotes.text_source_en: So, the student of war who is unversed in the art of war of varying his plans, even though he be acquainted with the Five Advantages, will fail to make the best use of his men.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 병법은 적이 오지 않으리라는 가능성에 기대지 말고 맞을 준비에 기대며, 적이 공격하지 않으리라는 우연에 기대지 말고 공격할 수 없는 태세에 기대라고 가르친다.
quotes.text_source_en: The art of war teaches us to rely not on the likelihood of the enemy’s not coming, but on our own readiness to receive him; not on the chance of his not attacking, but rather on the fact that we have made our position unassailable.
quotes.author: Sunzi (traditional attribution)
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 배는 적보다 상류에 대고 해를 마주하게 하라. 적을 만나려고 상류로 거슬러 올라가지 마라. 이것이 강에서 싸우는 법이다.

quotes.text_source_en: When a warlike prince attacks a powerful state, his generalship shows itself in preventing the concentration of the enemy’s forces. He overawes his opponents, and their allies are prevented from joining against him.

quotes.text_source_en: Sun Tzŭ said: There are five ways of attacking with fire. The first is to burn soldiers in their camp; the second is to burn stores; the third is to burn baggage-trains; the fourth is to burn arsenals and magazines; the fifth is to hurl dropping fire amongst the enemy.
